items.title: Mississauga approves 1-year moratorium on AI data centres
items.summary: Mississauga city council voted to approve a one-year moratorium on artificial intelligence data centres Wednesday, Global News reports. The move marks a departure from a pattern that had been forming across Ontario. A similar moratorium motion was defeated by Hamilton's city council earlier this month, and Vaughan has already approved a hyperscale AI data centre that is nearly finished construction and set to come online later this year. Mississauga's motion passed unanimously, though Mayor Carolyn Parrish did not cast a vote, since the mayor only votes to break a tie. At the centre of Wednesday's vote was a planned 50-100 megawatt site at Tenth Line West and Argentia Road, less than 300 metres from a residential neighbourhood. Both Mississauga and Ontario have been dotted with data centres for years, but this project, if built, would be among the province's first hyperscale facilities, drawing significantly more power than smaller sites and raising concerns about noise, water usage and grid capacity. The vote leaves it unclear if or how the project will now proceed. City councillor and mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo told Global News before the vote that more safeguards are needed, despite data centres' importance to the Canadian economy.

items.title: Is it safe to swim in Mississauga and Brampton? Here's what you need to know
items.summary: Residents looking to cool off in the water can head to Mississauga and Brampton beaches with confidence this week, as all four monitored swimming areas are currently safe for swimming, INsauga reports. The latest beach water testing results, released Wednesday, July 29, show acceptable bacteria levels at all public beaches monitored across the region. Peel Public Health tests water quality throughout the swimming season to help prevent illness and ensure recreational waters meet safety standards, with testing beginning in June and continuing until the end of the season. The all-clear comes as temperatures rise across the GTA and residents look for ways to beat the summer heat, though health officials continue to remind swimmers that conditions can change quickly, especially after heavy rainfall. High levels of bacteria in beach water can lead to illnesses including diarrhea, skin rashes, ear infections, eye irritation, coughing and congestion. Peel Public Health says bacteria levels can increase due to several factors, including heavy rain, stormwater runoff, large numbers of water birds, high winds, wave activity and large numbers of swimmers.

items.title: Temporary freeze put on any new AI data centres in Mississauga
items.summary: Plans to build any major data centres across Mississauga have been temporarily put on hold, giving the city more time to study the matter and draft new rules for the rapidly growing industry, INsauga reports. Following some two dozen deputations from residents and other stakeholders at Wednesday's city council meeting, the vast majority of whom spoke against the large new facilities, Mississauga councillors unanimously agreed to impose a moratorium of one year, extendable to two, on any such developments in the city. The motion, tabled by Ward 9 Coun. Martin Reid, sought to temporarily halt the development of major data centres in Mississauga by calling for an Interim Control Bylaw that would prohibit new large-scale digital infrastructure facilities, including artificial intelligence, cloud computing and hyperscale data centres, for up to one year while the city undertakes a comprehensive planning study. The pause applies citywide and can be extended to a second year if more time is needed to complete the review. Residents' fear of the unknown around huge data centres and their impact is understandable, Mayor Carolyn Parrish said following the vote. Wednesday's discussion, which took up most of the day inside council chamber at city hall, comes after months of growing concern among residents over a proposed Prologis data centre in Meadowvale.

items.title: Wild turkey sits on car, hangs out in Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: A wild turkey has been hanging around a Mississauga neighbourhood lately, sitting on cars and generally making itself at home, INsauga writes. A resident named Ricardo photographed the bird standing on top of a parked car and roaming around the neighbourhood, jokingly saying it is "protecting us from car theft." Community members first saw the wild turkey in the neighbourhood a few months ago, and it recently returned for what appears to be an extended stay. Residents have seen the bird frequently over the last few weeks, and a community member photographed it sitting on her bench and casually hanging out on a deck. Wild turkeys have become an increasingly common sight in parts of the GTA in recent years, as the population has rebounded and birds wander into residential areas in search of food. A City of Mississauga spokesperson confirmed that Animal Services received three reports of wild turkey sightings in the Hillcrest Avenue and Confederation Parkway area in April 2026.

items.title: Backyard fireworks not allowed over long weekend in Mississauga without a permit
items.summary: The Civic Holiday long weekend is just around the corner, but that does not mean Mississauga residents can celebrate with backyard fireworks without first obtaining a permit from the city, INsauga reports. While fireworks displays are permitted at people's homes in Mississauga without a permit on Victoria Day, Canada Day, Diwali, Lunar New Year and New Year's Eve, those who want to use the celebratory devices on their property this coming weekend to mark the Aug. 3 Civic Holiday must get prior permission from the municipality. The same permit rules also apply to the next long weekend, Labour Day, which falls in early September. In place of fireworks, City of Mississauga officials have suggested in past years that people celebrate in their backyards with glow sticks, noisemakers or sparklers instead. As usual on holiday weekends, Mississauga bylaw enforcement officers will be out in full force in the coming days to ensure fireworks are not being sold or used illegally. The city says Mississauga residents registered 58 fireworks use complaints with the bylaw enforcement department during the most-recent Canada Day holiday period, which ran from June 26 through July 2.

items.title: E-bike rider from Mississauga charged with impaired driving in another Ontario city
items.summary: A Mississauga man has been charged with impaired driving after Guelph police came across an e-bike rider who had fallen and hurt himself while operating the motorized vehicle on Tuesday night, INsauga reports. Investigation revealed the man was riding his e-bike when he lost control and fell over, with the bike falling on top of him, police said in a news release Wednesday, adding the rider was taken to hospital for treatment. While speaking to the man, the responding officer detected an odour of alcohol and noted signs of impairment. The man was arrested after failing a roadside breath test, and additional breath samples showed he had more than the legal amount of alcohol in his system, according to police. The 40-year-old is now charged with impaired driving, and his licence was suspended for 90 days. As e-bike use continues to grow across Ontario, police remind riders that the vehicles are subject to Highway Traffic Act rules and regulations and must follow the same rules of the road as cyclists.

items.title: Walmart Canada, Associates and Customers Raise $7.2 Million to Support Children's Hospitals Across Canada
items.summary: Walmart Canada and its associates and customers have raised $7.2 million to support children's hospital foundations across the country, Mississauga.com reports. The funds will help provide life-changing equipment, advance groundbreaking research, support specialized training and enhance programs that give children access to the care they need close to home. For more than 32 years, Walmart Canada, its associates and customers have supported Children's Miracle Network, raising and donating more than $250 million since 1994, with every dollar staying local to directly support children's hospital foundations in communities across Canada. Walmart associates played an important role in bringing this year's campaign to life, rallying support in stores and supply chain facilities across the country. Throughout the campaign, patient ambassadors visited Walmart stores across Canada to share their personal stories, helping associates and customers see the impact their donations make. Behind every donation, the company says, is a child and family whose life has changed because their local hospital had the right care, expertise and support when it mattered most.

items.title: Peel Region shelter crisis deepens as intimate partner violence incidents rise
items.summary: As intimate partner violence incidents rise in Peel Region, local leaders say provincially funded emergency shelters are becoming overburdened and hamstrung by outdated funding rules, CBC Toronto reports. The region's shelter system is struggling to accommodate the growing demand, with facilities operating beyond capacity while trying to provide essential services. Mississauga's mayor and the Peel Regional Council have called for increased provincial support and resources to address the crisis. The current funding model was designed years ago and fails to account for the complexity of modern cases requiring specialized trauma-informed care and longer-term support, advocates say. The situation highlights a critical gap between the rising need for safe housing and services for survivors of intimate partner violence and the resources currently available to support them in the community.

items.title: Mississauga councillor wants pause on AI data centres as Toronto councillors grapple with proposed facilities
items.summary: As communities across Canada and the United States deal with a surge in proposed AI data centres, councillors in the Greater Toronto Area are pushing for a more comprehensive response amid environmental concerns, CityNews Toronto writes. During a meeting of Mississauga city council on Wednesday, Coun. Martin Reid introduced a notice of motion calling for an interim control bylaw to stop the development of "major digital infrastructure facilities" for up to a year so City staff can conduct a planning study as well as a thorough review of bylaws and policies. CityNews met with Reid on Monday at the site of what he said would be the first massive, hyperscale data centre in the community. The site, located on Tenth Line west of Winston Churchill Boulevard and Highway 401 and near Lisgar GO station, sits next to a house, a church, greenspace and an existing warehouse. Just hundreds of metres away, though, there is a large shopping centre along with current and proposed housing subdivisions.

items.title: Child in critical condition after being rescued from pool at Mississauga home
items.summary: A child is in hospital in life-threatening condition after being rescued from a swimming pool in Mississauga on Tuesday morning, the Toronto Star reports. Emergency crews responded to a call for a reported drowning, and at the scene, a child was rescued from a residential swimming pool. A spokesperson for Peel Regional Paramedic Service said a young patient was brought to a local hospital in critical condition following the incident, and Peel paramedics provided emergency treatment and transport to assist with the response. Peel police spokesperson Laurie McCann told the Star that officers have no further information to provide at this time and asked that the family's privacy be respected during this difficult time. The incident marks another reminder of the importance of water safety and supervision around residential pools.

items.title: Peel Region confirms West Nile virus found in mosquitoes: What you need to know
items.summary: The first West Nile virus case of the year has been confirmed in Peel Region, the City of Mississauga announced. The mosquitoes carrying the virus were identified in Brampton near the intersection of Queen Street East and Kennedy Road North, and with the virus now active locally, residents are advised to take steps to protect themselves and their property from infected insects. West Nile virus is a mosquito-borne illness that can cause mild flu-like symptoms in most people, but in rare cases it can lead to serious illness affecting the brain or nervous system, and there is no vaccine or specific treatment for humans, making prevention essential. People over 50 or with weakened immune systems face a higher risk of serious complications, city health officials note. Mosquitoes that transmit West Nile virus are most active at dusk and dawn, so limiting exposure during peak hours or staying indoors during those times can help. Residents are urged to eliminate standing water on their property, since mosquitoes need only a few millimetres of stagnant water to breed.
